turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_target_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_target_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have a yield strength CLOSEST to 1051 MPa — not the highest, the closest to that value — then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**1. Processing dominates.** Group means of `target`:

| heat_treatment | ≈ mean |
|---|---|
| quench_temper | ~590 |
| solution_aged | ~490 |
| quenched | ~435 |
| annealed | ~350 |

Within `quench_temper`, route matters too: **wrought ≈ 640 > cast ≈ 590 > AM ≈ 530**. Essentially every training point above 700 MPa is `quench_temper` (usually *wrought*): 863.9, 734.1, 726.4, 721.6, 737.7, 709.2, 908.5 (AM outlier).

**2. Composition: "moderate everything" wins, saturated recipes lose.**
All the very low targets (140–280 MPa) are rows sitting on several upper bounds simultaneously (C 1.2, Mn 2, Si 1.5, Mo 6, V 1.5, Nb 1, Al 2, Ti 1.5, Cu 3, Co 15, Cr 22). Group contrasts inside `quench_temper`:

* Cr 8–16 → mean ≈ 650; Cr ≥ 18 → mean ≈ 460 (strong penalty)
* Mo ≥ 5 → mean ≈ 476 (≈ –30 MPa per extra %Mo)
* Ti ≥ 1.4, Si = 1.5, Cu = 3, Al ≈ 2, Co = 15, C ≥ 0.9 all shift the mean down 45–130 MPa
* Best cells: Cr ≈ 9–16, Ni ≈ 8–15, Co ≈ 4–8, Mo ≈ 1–2.5, C ≈ 0.2–0.6, with Si/Al/Ti/Mn/Nb/V/Cu kept small (e.g. the 726, 734, 737, 864 MPa rows).

**3. Target 1051 MPa is above the training maximum (908 MPa).** So the task reduces to picking the pool recipes with the **highest expected strength** — i.e. quench-tempered, wrought, Cr ≈ 10–14, Ni ≈ 10–14, Co ≈ 5–7, Mo ≈ 2, C ≈ 0.3–0.6, and no elements pinned at their bounds. (Processing terms — aging temp 480–610 °C, long-ish aging, high cooling — give only a modest extra push.)

**4. Screening the pool.** The heavily saturated candidates (c016, c029, c046, c050, c051, c058, c073, c088, c096), all annealed/quenched ones (c072, c091, c018, c084, c020…) and the Cr ≥ 18 / Mo ≥ 5 ones (c081, c078, c062, c047) are predicted low. The best-profile group is the clean quench-temper + wrought family:

| cand | Cr | Ni | Co | Mo | C | notes | pred |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c097 | 13.2 | 13.5 | 5.2 | 2.0 | 0.26 | very clean (Al 0.13, Ti 0.28, Cu 0.09) — twin of the 726 MPa row | ~700 |
| c049 | 9.5 | 11.2 | 5.6 | 2.0 | 0.58 | balanced optimum | ~690 |
| c085 | 11.9 | 12.5 | 6.2 | 1.9 | 0.54 | balanced optimum | ~685 |
| c099 | 8.5 | 8.2 | 6.3 | 1.9 | 0.43 | low Al/Ti | ~685 |
| c017 | 7.7 | 10.1 | 0.9 | 1.4 | 0.33 | nearly identical to the 864 MPa training row | ~680 |
| c069/c082/c052/c059 | — | — | — | — | — | same family, slightly more Al/Si/Mo | ~670 |

These are the only candidates whose predicted strength approaches the 700–900 MPa band, hence the smallest |prediction – 1051|.

**Final: c097, c049, c085, c099, c017**
